claims.claim: Reviewers state that logic blocks and game mechanics lack proper in-game guides or explanations, requiring external research or trial and error.

citations.review_text:
This is a great game. Anyone who dreams to race / fly / fight etc with the vehicles they've designed, this is a go to game. I've finished the single player scenario, which is like a nice, small, intro to the game. Also player a couple of multiplayer rounds with my son. It's like playing with legos together, but you can be much more creative.

There are a few issues, I hope the developers solve:
1- A proper in game guide to how each logic and sensor block works, in detail, with all the option within the block explained, with multiple examples. Currently there are some confusing blocks, like the AND block, it's not actually an AND block (what programmers understand from AND), it's a conditional SUM block with a multiplier at the end. 
2- Some missing logic blocks, like a proper clamp block could be handy.
3- I wish there was a panel that shows which blocks are taking how many power cores. This would be like a summary to quickly see where the player is spending their power core budget. It would be opened by clicking the total power value on the top right, and would group the blocks in categories. Like I'm spending 14 power on weapons; these are 2 submachine gun 2x2 =4  ... etc.

Overall great game, and I think it has a great play time * fun / price value.

(Playing on Legion Go 2 with it's own controllers. Runs good.)

6.5/10

Basically a Lego video game, with a strong community, and single player mode so you can just take your time and enjoy being creative.  Offline functionality means when servers shut down someday, you should still be able to play the game.

The reason it's not 10/10, is questionable physics.  Despite how long the game has been developed, and added on to, the physics and logic can be very buggy, and some mechanics aren't very well explained, leaving you to either experiment just to figure it out, or look up a wiki, which I feel shouldn't be necessary.  Tool tips are missing for logic block advanced settings, and even when you think you understand how one works, it can sometimes break, and behave weirdly, like output from a logic block getting stuck, and not resetting.  This unreliable feature mixed with the buggy physics, means sometimes your creation suddenly explodes, goes spinning, or thrown into space for no explainable reason.  I'm just disappointed that after all the development and updates, the core mechanics are still plagued with bugs.

All this being said, the game is chill, no real risk, or competition, so when a bug occurs, it's very easy to just shrug it off, cause you most likely didn't lose anything.  Sometimes the randomness itself can be a source of amusement, like cartoon comedy.

Bottom line, definitely a game I recommend, though it has it's flaws.

claims.claim: Reviewers report a lack of variety in certain parts, specifically noting missing sizing options for streamlining blocks, wedges, and panels.

citations.review_text: they just need to add 9 x9 and 1x1 blocks and panels then it would be better

This game is a great one if you're looking for a game about building stuff, but with enough added goodies to keep you hooked for hours on end. It's absolutely worth the price tag, if not even more than that, and I find myself anticipating the day where I can finally get the Collector's Bundle.

I do, however, have a tiny problem. There aren't nearly enough varieties of streamlining block. Sure, it wouldn't be a problem to any casual player, but if someone needs, say, a 1x1x2 Wedge Corner, or some other wedge corner in some other dimensionality, it'll be a pain to work around a lack of such, especially for more angular builds like a rugged prototype for an amphibious mobile base.

That could just be a me problem, though. Either way, the game's more than enough fun to make up for such an issue. I'd recommend this game for anyone that wants a good gameplay experience with enough campaign content to knock their socks off.

good game but has a few major flaws that limit creativity,

1-Lots of expensive DLC with blocks kind of essential for many different builds

2-Game has a large amount of bugs so normalized they are used in building and tend to make it much more frustrating, like logic being half broken and only working sometimes.

3-General lack of building blocks make it quite difficult to make anything look nice without extensive game knowledge and time, along with luck for certain glitches

This game is really fun. The pvp is generally chill, the vehicles are fun to pilot the damge system is good and it generally allows you to do what you want. As long as what you want is to build a completly normal plane/car that is withing a very specific size criteria. if you want to build a mech that isnt just a helicopter with fake legs it will cause SOMETHING to clip into something else cause the vehicle to detonate. if you make wings that can swing back it will sometimes stop working or something will clip causing the plane to explode. If you want large turrets the aiming servos might just turn off for no reason. To make the plane go fast you need to fill the entire volume of the plane with servos. And the game is so unoptimized a fighter jet will easily reach the default part cap for the game and if you use a mod to go past that random parts will just MOVE OUT OF PLACE AND CLIP INTO EACH OTHER AND JUST EXPLODE.

Like someone once said: "The only limit, is your limited imagination." and it's rather true. If you look past the bugs and technical issues, it is a great game. Idea, experiment and optimize is how i describe the gameplay, you have an idea, you experiment with it and learn things from it and then you optimize the build to perfection. DLCs can be very nice to have but not many people will know which ones are good, so i will give you a list of ones i recommend: Motorhead DLC: Gives a good amount of things to play around with my favourite being the large spring. Mech amok DLC: Grants a bunch of decorative blocks that i use alot not just on mechs, and the mech feet are so powerful. Frontline pack DLC: Gives different blocks new skins like turning the smart cannon into a browning machine gun, also makes the engines sound more like actual engines. Packing heat DLC: Weapons and more weapons, and a propeller engine i don't know why there's an engine in it but it's there. And finally the Space voyager DLC: The glow decals have been used so much it's insane. Do remember that DLCs aren't necessary, you decide if you need them. With that being said, have a great day and happy trailmaking!
